items.heading: Trading Financial Markets Full
items.text: Trading financial markets full-time is a real, legal, legitimate way some people earn a living in India. It is also, by the regulator's own measurement, a path where the large majority of people who attempt it lose money, and keep losing money even after years of trying.

items.heading: "Is Trading a Good Career"
items.text: "Is trading a good career" usually gets asked as one question, but it hides two genuinely different paths that share a word and almost nothing else. Confusing them is where a lot of the damage happens.

rows: 89% of individual equity F&O traders had net losses
SEBI's first large-scale study on this, covering roughly 90 lakh individual traders across major brokers.
93% of individual traders lost money; only 7.2% were profitable
Cumulative net losses across all individual F&O traders exceeded Rs 1.8 lakh crore over the three years, including transaction costs.
Rs 74,812 crore net loss for individual traders
Average loss per losing trader was about Rs 1.20 lakh that year; average profit per winning trader was lower, about Rs 1.03 lakh.
Losses widened 41% to Rs 1,05,603 crore; 91%+ still lost money
Unique traders fell about 20% year-on-year after SEBI's own curbs, fewer weekly expiries and higher minimum lot sizes, pushed some smaller traders out.

items.heading: Retail Self
items.text: Retail self-directed trading: you open a demat and trading account, fund it with your own savings, and trade on your own judgment. Every rupee of risk is yours. This is what almost all "how to become a trader" content online is actually about.

items.heading: Professional or Institutional Trading
items.text: Professional or institutional trading: you are hired, often after a quantitative or finance-heavy hiring process, into a role at a proprietary trading firm, hedge fund, brokerage, or bank. You earn a salary (often with performance-linked pay), and the firm's capital, not yours, is what is at risk on most positions.

items.heading: Both Are Legitimate
items.text: Both are legitimate. But the skills, risk, income structure, and entry path are different enough that advice for one rarely transfers cleanly to the other.
